profile.summary: RNAErnie is an RNA language model that turns an RNA sequence into embeddings for downstream prediction. During pretraining it uses known RNA motifs as prior knowledge and masks them at random, alongside the usual masked language modelling. Its developers fine-tune it for RNA sequence classification, RNA-RNA interaction prediction and RNA secondary structure prediction.

summary_quotes.text: This repository contains codes and pre-trained models for RNAErnie, which leverages RNA motifs as **biological priors** and proposes a **motif-level random masking** strategy to enhance pre-training tasks.

Furthermore, RNAErnie improves sequence classfication, RNA-RNA interaction prediction, and RNA secondary structure prediction by fine-tuning or adapating on downstream tasks with two-stage **type-guided** learning.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The original RNAErnie is a 12-layer ERNIE transformer with hidden size 768, written in PaddlePaddle. It is pretrained on about 23 million RNAcentral ncRNA sequences of up to 512 nucleotides with three masking levels, chosen at random in a 1:1:1 ratio: base-level masking of 15% of nucleotides, masking of contiguous subsequences of 4 to 8 bases, and motif-level masking of motifs gathered from ATtRACT, SpliceAid and the most frequent 4 to 8 base sequences in RNAcentral. An [IND] token followed by the sequence's RNA type is appended during pretraining. For downstream tasks the paper offers a frozen backbone with a trainable head (FBTH), a trainable backbone and head (TBTH), and a two-stage type-guided STACK design that first predicts the top-K RNA types, appends each to the sequence and averages the K predictions weighted by their probabilities. For secondary structure prediction it computes four folding scores per base pair and decodes with Zuker-style dynamic programming, using a module compiled from mxfold2. Pretraining ran about 2,580,000 steps with batch size 50 on four Nvidia Tesla V100 32 GB GPUs for around 250 hours. The authors' later PyTorch checkpoint is a separate BERT masked language model with 12 layers, hidden size 768, 12 attention heads and an 11-token vocabulary.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are two lines of checkpoints. The original PaddlePaddle model from the paper, with masking-strategy variants and task-specific fine-tuned weights, is distributed through Google Drive folders linked from the README; an ad-hoc variant pretrained with an extra classification loss and a 1-epoch checkpoint are also linked. In June 2024 the developers trained a separate PyTorch model from scratch with a maximum length of 2048 on a newer RNAcentral release of about 31 million sequences, and published it on Hugging Face (now LLM-EDA/RNAErnie); its tokenisation differs slightly from the original. A result should say which of these checkpoints was used.

run_guide.summary: Set up the original PaddlePaddle RNAErnie environment and extract embeddings for three example RNA sequences with the pretrained checkpoint.
prerequisites: Conda, and a GPU: the environment installs paddlepaddle-gpu 2.3.2 and the example sets the device to gpu.

The pretrained checkpoint files (.pdparams and .json) downloaded by hand from the Google Drive folder linked in the README and placed in ./output/BERT,ERNIE,MOTIF,PROMPT so that output/BERT,ERNIE,MOTIF,PROMPT/checkpoint_final/ exists. The README does not state the folder layout inside the download.
The environment file pins Linux conda builds and a Tsinghua mirror channel, so it may not resolve on other platforms.

steps.title: Extract embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import paddle
from rna_ernie import BatchConverter
from paddlenlp.transformers import ErnieModel

# ========== Set device
paddle.set_device("gpu")

# ========== Prepare Data
data = [
    ("RNA1", "GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGGGAAGUCCUCGUGUUGCACCCCU"),
    ("RNA2", "GGGUGUCGCUCAGUUGGUAGAGUGCUUGCCUGGCAUGCAAGAAACCUUGGUUCAAUCCCCAGCACUGCA"),
    ("RNA3", "CGAUUCNCGUUCCC--CCGCCUCCA"),
]

# ========== Batch Converter
batch_converter = BatchConverter(k_mer=1,
                                  vocab_path="./data/vocab/vocab_1MER.txt",
                                  batch_size=256,
                                  max_seq_len=512)

# ========== RNAErnie Model
rna_ernie = ErnieModel.from_pretrained("output/BERT,ERNIE,MOTIF,PROMPT/checkpoint_final/")
rna_ernie.eval()

# call batch_converter to convert sequences to batch inputs
for names, _, inputs_ids in batch_converter(data):
    with paddle.no_grad():
        # extract whole sequence embeddings
        embeddings = rna_ernie(inputs_ids)[0].detach()
        # extract [CLS] token embedding
        embeddings_cls = embeddings[:, 0, :]
        print(names, embeddings.shape, embeddings_cls.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README's embedding example, run from the repository root and wrapped in a heredoc; the commented-out FASTA line was dropped and a print of the names and tensor shapes was added.

outputs: Whole-sequence token embeddings and [CLS] embeddings for each batch of input sequences, held as Paddle tensors.

notes: The README names two Hugging Face copies: the authors' PyTorch model (WANGNingroci/RNAErnie, which now redirects to LLM-EDA/RNAErnie) and a third-party port at multimolecule/rnaernie, which was not used as a source. Which checkpoint the You et al. 2026 benchmark used should be checked against that paper before linking results. The paper's full text is now saved and quoted from its pdftotext layer; the PDF is two-column, so quotes are kept within one column line. The paper is CC BY 4.0, but store_bytes is false as the revision brief asks. No IP-address stamp was found in the text layer.
